lines.text: Every soul in Saltmouth came out that night, and all sixty of ours. The fog was so thick, I could barely see the tower.
Here goes, my lord! If I explode, tell my apprentices they were all terrible!
The light came on like a second moon. It cut the fog in half, and swept across the sea, and there were the Teeth, black and wet and plain as day.
Smoke in my eyes. Don't look at me.
Pell. Are you sure they're coming?
Captain Ressa owes me three hundred crowns, my lord. People who owe me money always come back. Usually to borrow more.
Just before midnight, a lantern appeared in the fog. Then sails. A Vask ship, threading our new channel as neat as a needle.
Thirty years, nobody's docked at Saltmouth. Who lit that thing?
A zero.
A zero? Then gods help us all when he learns to count.
By dawn, Saltmouth had sold more fish than in the last ten years, and the ship's hold was full of Deep rimeglass. The Senn had nothing to do with any of it.
In Saltmouth, we don't kneel to lords. We give them salt from the pans. If they spit it out, they go home.
It was the saltiest thing I have ever tasted. I swallowed it anyway.
Then you're ours. Or we're yours. It's all the same, out here.
Forty-one new threads ran out of me at once. Cold, and salty as the sea.
At that same moment, two days away, the lamp in Greyhollow's hall jumped. Bram was the only one there to see it.
Two days later, a rider brought me a letter from Bram. One line.
The lamp jumped. I was not talking to it.
Your Root just went deeper. The ceiling is still five. But everyone under it will grow faster now. Saltmouth too.
Vask will buy every lamp you can make, my lord. But not one counting house will hold your money. House Corrow pays them very well not to.
Then we'll open our own.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter forty-six, coming soon.
